# Dimension: Platform Overview, Licensing, Community

Reference file for [citations.md](../citations.md).

## What Hatchet Is

Hatchet is a distributed, fault-tolerant task queue and workflow orchestration
platform built on PostgreSQL [1][2]. Written primarily in Go, it provides SDKs
for Python, TypeScript, Go, and Ruby [1][10]. The platform bundles a task queue,
observability, alerting, web dashboard, and CLI into a single deployable system [10].

Hatchet can function as a queue, a DAG-based orchestrator, a durable execution
engine, or all three simultaneously [1]. Three primary concepts structure the
platform [1]:

| Concept | Description | Source |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| Tasks | Fundamental work units wrapping functions | [1] |
| Workers | Long-running processes that execute tasks | [1] |
| Durable Workflows | Composed multi-task pipelines with dependencies and checkpointing | [1] |

## Architecture

Four core components [2]:

| Component | Role | Source |
|-----------|------|--------|
| API Server | Entry point; handles workflow triggers, state queries, UI, webhook ingestion | [2] |
| Engine | Orchestration layer; evaluates dependencies, enforces policies, schedules/dispatches tasks | [2] |
| Workers | User-operated processes; connect to engine, execute code, report results | [2] |
| Storage | PostgreSQL as durable source of truth; optional RabbitMQ for higher throughput | [2] |

Workers connect to the engine via bidirectional gRPC for "low-latency dispatch
and frequent status updates" [2]. State is persisted transactionally in
PostgreSQL [2].

## Positioning vs Competitors

Hatchet positions itself as a general-purpose task orchestration platform competing
with Temporal (durable execution), Celery/pg-boss (task queues), and Airflow/Prefect
(DAG orchestration) [1][21][24].

Key differentiators claimed [21][24]:
- PostgreSQL-only infrastructure (vs Temporal's multiple database backends)
- Bundled observability and dashboard (vs Temporal's separate monitoring)
- Simpler self-hosting than Temporal
- MIT license (vs Temporal's MIT but more complex deployment)

## Gaps and Limitations

- **Young project**: Founded 2023, first public release March 2024 [11][24]
- **Small team**: 7 employees [11]
- **No named enterprise adopters** found in search results
- **V1 rewrite**: Major architecture rewrite underway as of 2025 [24]
- **Limited contributor diversity**: Most commits likely from founding team
